security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel trap entry/exit code on RISC-V executes the Smip context save/restore sequence (saving registers then adjusting sp) but either (a) reorders register saves after the stack pointer adjustment, or (b) fails to handle the case where a synchronous exception during save leaves xepc pointing to the original trap rather than the faulting instruction, causing resumption at a stale context and potential double-execution or register corruption on the return path
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: sp adjustment before full register save in trap entry; assumption that mid-save faults are unrecoverable without checking double-trap capability; missing misa.Smip or double-trap feature test before emitting Smip-style save sequences
security_spec.summary: Smip context-save faults set xepc to the original trap PC (not the fault PC), so unless the kernel's entry code preserves the ordering guarantee (registers-before-sp) and verifies double-trap support, a mid-save exception corrupts resumed state

findings.finding: sp adjusted BEFORE full register save (addi sp, sp, -(PT_SIZE_ON_STACK) at line 163, then REG_S saves at lines 164-167). The Smip-compliant sequence requires saving registers before adjusting sp. If this kernel runs on Smip-capable hardware, a mid-save synchronous exception leaves SCRATCH holding user_tp (line 200 csrw CSR_SCRATCH,x0 not yet reached), causing the re-entered trap handler to use user's tp as thread pointer at line 161, leading to register corruption and potential kernel info leak into userspace memory.
findings.snippet:
.Lsave_context:
	REG_S sp, TASK_TI_USER_SP(tp)
	REG_L sp, TASK_TI_KERNEL_SP(tp)
	addi sp, sp, -(PT_SIZE_ON_STACK)
	REG_S x1,  PT_RA(sp)
	...
	csrw CSR_SCRATCH, x0

findings.finding: Same sp-before-save pattern as handle_exception: addi sp, sp, -(PT_SIZE_ON_STACK) at line 332 before REG_S x1/x3/x5 and save_from_x6_to_x31 at lines 335-338. No double-trap guard on the overflow stack path. If the overflow stack page faults during the save sequence, no recovery mechanism exists (unlike the main path which has new_vmalloc_check).
findings.snippet:
addi sp, sp, -(PT_SIZE_ON_STACK)

//save context to overflow stack
REG_S x1,  PT_RA(sp)
REG_S x3,  PT_GP(sp)
REG_S x5,  PT_T0(sp)
save_from_x6_to_x31

findings.finding: new_vmalloc_check macro handles vmalloc page faults during trap entry by doing sret (line 85) to retry the faulting instruction. On Smip hardware where save sequence reordering matters, this re-execution is blind: it does not check whether preceding instructions in the save sequence (like csrrc CSR_STATUS at line 183) have side effects that make re-execution non-idempotent. The sret also does not verify that the re-executed save sequence hasn't been corrupted by a first partial pass.
findings.snippet:
REG_L	a0, TASK_TI_A0(tp)
REG_L	a1, TASK_TI_A1(tp)
REG_L	a2, TASK_TI_A2(tp)
csrw	CSR_SCRATCH, x0
sret

findings.finding: CSR_SCRATCH cleared to 0 at line 200 AFTER all CSR saves (lines 183-194) but BEFORE the actual exception dispatch (line 212+). If a trap occurs between lines 200-211 (e.g., during scs_load_current or v_context_nesting_start), the recursive kernel trap is detected (scratch==0) but xepc points to the instruction in that window, not the original user instruction. The ret_from_exception path would then sret to a kernel address with user-privilege context (if the original trap was from user mode), or skip the user-return setup at lines 262-273 entirely, corrupting the SCRATCH→tp mapping for the next user entry.

CSR_STATUS restored (line 301) before CSR_EPC restored (line 302). On Smip hardware, restoring STATUS first may re-enable interrupts or change privilege mode bits before EPC is valid. If an interrupt fires between the two CSR writes, the interrupted context has a stale EPC pointing to the previous (to-be-discarded) trap frame rather than the correct return address. This is a TOCTOU hazard in the restore sequence.
findings.snippet:
csrw CSR_STATUS, a0
csrw CSR_EPC, a2

REG_L x1,  PT_RA(sp)

findings.finding: Only one trap vector (handle_exception) installed via csrw CSR_TVEC at boot and secondary CPU startup. No Smip-specific trap vector and no misa.Smip/misa.Sdt capability check anywhere in the kernel. The SBI_FWFT_DOUBLE_TRAP (0x3) enum is defined (include/asm/sbi.h:429) but has no implementation — KVM reports it as unsupported. If hardware supports Smip/Smrnmi, the kernel has no code path to install the alternate trap vector or enable the double-trap mechanism.
findings.snippet:
.Lsetup_trap_vector:
	la a0, handle_exception
	csrw CSR_TVEC, a0
	csrw CSR_SCRATCH, zero
	ret

findings.finding: KVM VM-exit path restores host CSR_STVEC (line 152) BEFORE saving guest CSR_SEPC (line 149). The code reads guest SEPC into t1 at line 139, then writes host STVEC at line 152, and only then stores t1 (guest SEPC) to memory at line 163. If a trap occurs between the host STVEC write and the SEPC store, the host exception handler may clobber t1, losing the guest's EPC value. This violates the Smip principle of saving all CSRs before restoring any CSR that could change the trap delivery target.
findings.snippet:
csrr	t1, CSR_SEPC
...
csrw	CSR_STVEC, t0
...
REG_S	t1, VCPU_ARCH_SEPC(s0)
